newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bears come out of woods to maul Belgian shares.
newsitem.headline: Bears come out of woods to maul Belgian shares.

text.p: The bears came out of the woods to maul Belgian shares on Tuesday as European bond yields rose on monetary union jitters and the dollar slipped.

The Bel-20 index ended 32.29 points, or 1.49 percent, lower at 2,138.66 points with over five billion Belgian francs of shares traded. Cement maker CBR was the only Bel-20 issue to end in positive territory.

Dealers said the technical picture for the Bel-20 was now very negative and a recovery would be dependent on a reversal in the upward movement in interest rates that took the yield on 10-year OLOs to above 6.00 percent on Tuesday.
"We have closed below the (Bel-20's) 20-day moving average, which was close to resistance around 2,150 (points). Now we are below it's very, very negative," one trader said.

"On Friday I thought we would be flat with a positive bias, but after the comments yesterday from (German Finance Minister Theo Waigel), the rise in interest rates, the lower dollar and the jitters on Wall Street, it does not look good," he added.
"Everything now depends on interest rates. If Germany does not look like fulfilling the criteria for the euro that puts pressure on everybody," another trader agreed.
Tuesday's losses were across the board, with both industrials and interest-rate sensitive stocks suffering.
Insurer Royale Belge, the star performer of the last two sessions, ended down 310 francs, or 3.37 percent at 8,890 francs.
Glassmaker Glaverbel, which lies outside the Bel-20, fell 140 francs, or 3.28 percent to 4,130 francs.
Steel wire and cord maker Bekaert, which is due to release 1996 results on Wednesday, fell 350 francs to 21,575 francs.
